description.narrative: The objective of the Haiphong Urban Transport Development Project for Vietnam is to improve urban accessibility and strengthen capacity for urban transport management and planning in Haiphong. There are three components to the project, the first component being urban main road development. This component will increase urban accessibility through construction of a new east-west link (connected to main north-south links) for cross town traffic within Haiphong and longer distance freight to and from Haiphong's port system. The second component is the transport improvement. This component supports transformation of the public transportation services along the Tam Bac-Kien an urban corridor, including measures to strengthen institutional development for public transport management, piloting of transformative approaches to fleet management, acquisition of new buses, and upgrading of infrastructure and facilities. Finally, the third component is the capacity-building.
The project development objective is to improve urban accessibility and strengthen capacity for urban transport management and planning in Haiphong.

title.narrative: Increase number of passenger on Bus line 2

comment.narrative:
<p>This Indicator reported as text should have been reported as number (passengers per day). This indicator is duplicated in the intermediate indicators, and an explanation is not evident.</p>
<p>The indicator did not specify the methodology nor it specified what constitutes a day (time) or if the indicator is an average of weekday/weekend or just weekday. It is unclear if the indicator measures total boardings along the route for the total operating time of the services, or if it only measures boardings at the terminal station. Considering there are three lines serving the terminal (02, 2.1, 2.2), the indicator could have specified if it was adding the total number of routes or disaggregated by bus route. The M&E did not explain the methodology to measure passenger volumes, so the author assumes boardings counts along the route as per guidelines from the US DOT National Transit Database Sampling Manual, available at https://www.transit.dot.gov/sites/fta.dot.gov/files/docs/The_NTD_Sampling_Manual.pdf</p>

title.narrative: reduced traffic volume on NH5-Nam Hai

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator tracks changes in traffic volumes, disaggregated by cars, trucks, and motorcycles, on two segments. The title of the indicator includes the direction of change (reduction), whereas best practice recommends not signaling the desired direction of change on the indicator name but on the target. The indicator counts traffic volumes from cars, trucks, buses, and motorbikes, without making it clear that it aims at an overall reduction in traffic volumes, lineally adding all vehicle categories. in this sense, an increase in private cars paired with a reduction in trucks is tracked as positive as long as the total volume is less than the baseline. This is contrary to best practices, where different vehicle categories have different weights to produce aggregate volume levels.</p>

<p>The targets were not met, as overall vehicle volumes increased by 1.5 (NH10-Quan Tru ) and 2x (Quan Tru -Nam Hai).</p>

<p>For NH10-Quan Tru and Quan Tru-Nam Hai, volumes for cars increased by 1.4 and 3.3, respectively, truck levels by 1.77 and 2.19, and motorcycles by 1.46 and 1.87. Volumes for buses were reduced 61 and 26 percent, respectively, without an explanation for this (bus restructuring, rerouting, decommissioning of routes). </p>

<p>Overall, this indicator is confusing, poorly formulated and the resulting output opposes the desired one. </p>
